[[Aston, Pennsylvania]] }} '''Tyreke Evans''' (born [[September 19]], [[1989]]) is an American [[basketball]] player. He is a 6'6" [[shooting guard]] and plays for the [[Memphis Tigers basketball|University of Memphis]]. He has since become the starting [[point guard]] for the Tigers. He is widely considered one of the best players from his 2008 high school class and a potential lottery pick in the NBA draft.{{cite web | url=http://www.nbadraftdepot.com/2009/01/2009-nba-mock-draft.html| title=Draft Depot - 2009 NBA Mock Draft | publisher = | accessdate=2009-03-13}} ==High school== Evans grew up in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]], and was mainly raised by his three older brothers.Jere Longman. "[http://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/21/sports/ncaabasketball/21preps.html Prep Star's Rise Aided by His Brother's Best Intentions]". ''[[New York Times]]''. [[February 21]],[[2008]]. Retrieved on [[June 25]], [[2008]]. He attended [[American Christian Academy]] in [[Aston, Pennsylvania]], and by his sophomore year began drawing comparisons to [[NBA All-Star]] [[Tracy McGrady]].Mark Beech and Ted Keith. "[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/magazine/06/26/where.will.they.be0703/index.html Where Will They Be?]" ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''. [[June 27]], [[2006]]. Retrieved on [[June 25]], [[2008]]. As a senior, he averaged 32.1 [[points per game]] and was named the Most Valuable Player of the [[McDonald's All-American Game]], where he posted 21 points, 10 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 4 [[assists]] to help lead the East team to a 107-102 victory over the West. At the age of 16, he was featured in the documentary "Gunning for That #1 Spot" directed by [[MCA (musician)|Adam "MCA" Yauch]] of the [[Beastie Boys]].http://www.imdb.com/name/nm0946888/ ==SLAM Magazine== Evans was chosen to be the keeper of the [[SLAM Magazine]] High School Diary for the 2008 season.http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SLAM_Magazine ==College== In April 2008, Evans announced that he would attend the University of Memphis, after also considering [[Villanova University]] and the [[University of Texas]]."[http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=400780 Tyreke Evans picks Memphis Tigers]". [[Associated Press]]. ''[[The Sporting News]]''. [[April 16]], [[2008]]. Retrieved on [[June 25]], [[2008]]. Evans struggled at times at the beginning of his freshman season until coach [[John Calipari]] inserted him as the starting point guard in the 11th game of the season, a 60-45 win over the [[University of Cincinnati]]. In 33 minutes, Evans nearly put up a triple-double, with 14 points, 10 rebounds, and eight assists.http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/dec/29/tigers-take-down-bearcats-60-45-despite-cold-start/ The Tigers would not lose another game until falling to the [[Missouri Tigers]] in the [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. Through February 23rd, following conference victories against [[SMU]] and [[UTEP]], Evans was named the [[Conference USA]] Rookie of the Week eight times.http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2009/feb/09/lucky-7-conference-usa-honors-tigers-evans-seventh/?feedback=1#comments Evans was the only freshman finalist for the 2009 [[U.S. Basketball Writers of America]] National Player of the year award, named in honor of [[Oscar Robertson]]. ==NBA== On March 31, 2009, Evans declared himself eligible for the [[2009 NBA Draft]], where he is a potential lottery selection.
